quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Win' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To achieve what you wanted.
quests.contextSentence: With steady effort, learners ___ in speaking clearly.
quests.usageExample: With steady effort, learners succeed in speaking clearly.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Win' takes prizes and races (`win gold`). 'Succeed' succeeds in goals, careers, or hard plans (`succeed in coding`).
quests.explanation: Natural — accomplishing challenging goals takes 'succeed'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ in coding" — starts with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Fail' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To not achieve or catch something.
quests.contextSentence: Watch the street numbers carefully so you do not ___ our turn.
quests.usageExample: Watch the street numbers carefully so you do not miss our turn.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Fail' marks unsuccessful tests or machine breakdowns (`brakes fail`). 'Miss' reaches slightly too late (`miss the bus`, `miss the target`).
quests.explanation: Natural — arriving late or overlooking something takes 'miss'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ the bus" — starts with 'M'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Solve' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To find an answer or settle trouble.
quests.contextSentence: Support managers work fast to ___ billing complaints.
quests.usageExample: Support managers work fast to resolve billing complaints.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Solve' figures out math, riddles, and crimes. 'Resolve' peacefully settles arguments, conflicts, or delays.
quests.explanation: Natural — settling human conflicts or issues uses 'resolve'.
quests.hint: 'Solve' figures out math, riddles, and crimes — think of the 'Team Conflict' sense starting with 'R'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Book' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To arrange a seat, room, or time early.
quests.contextSentence: Always ___ museum time slots online during summer.
quests.usageExample: Always reserve museum time slots online during summer.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Book' fits travel tickets and hotels (`book a flight`). 'Reserve' stresses holding something aside strictly for you (`reserve a corner booth`).
quests.explanation: Natural — setting a specific booth or time slot aside takes 'reserve'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ a corner booth" — starts with 'R'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Order' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To tell someone what to do or send.
quests.contextSentence: Generals rarely ___ without clear maps first.
quests.usageExample: Generals rarely command without clear maps first.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Order' covers restaurant food and packages (`order soup`). 'Command' carries military or authoritative control.
quests.explanation: Natural — authority over troops or ships takes 'command'.
quests.hint: 'Order' covers restaurant food and packages (`order soup`) — think of the 'Rescue Ship' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Wait' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To stay or look ahead to something.
quests.contextSentence: Economists ___ steadier fuel prices next spring.
quests.usageExample: Economists expect steadier fuel prices next spring.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Wait' marks physical passing of minutes (`wait here`). 'Expect' thinks something will probably arrive (`expect guests`).
quests.explanation: Natural — believing/anticipating an arrival uses 'expect'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ guests" — starts with 'E'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Watch' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To pay attention with your eyes.
quests.contextSentence: Students used lenses to ___ tiny crystals forming.
quests.usageExample: Students used lenses to observe tiny crystals forming.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Watch' follows changing action (`watch hockey`). 'Observe' studies behavior scientifically or respects rules/holidays (`observe traffic rules`).
quests.explanation: Natural — careful scientific study takes 'observe'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ traffic rules" — starts with 'O'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Push' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To apply force against something.
quests.contextSentence: Gently ___ the seal until the lunchbox clicks shut.
quests.usageExample: Gently press the seal until the lunchbox clicks shut.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Push' moves heavy carts, swings, or people forward (`push the trolley`). 'Press' pushes flat switches, elevator buttons, or clothes cleanly.
quests.explanation: Natural — finger-tapping flat switches and keys takes 'press'.
quests.hint: 'Push' moves heavy carts, swings, or people forward (`push the trolley`) — think of the 'Lift Button' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Turn' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To change angle or go around.
quests.contextSentence: Children watched colorful pinwheels ___ in the breeze.
quests.usageExample: Children watched colorful pinwheels spin in the breeze.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Turn' covers steering, pages, and turning 90°. 'Spin' rotates rapidly round and round (`bicycle wheel spins`).
quests.explanation: Natural — fast full rotations use 'spin'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "bicycle wheel ___s" — starts with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Plain' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Relaxed and comfortable without dressy fuss.
quests.contextSentence: They held a warm, ___ dinner on the porch.
quests.usageExample: They held a warm, casual dinner on the porch.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Plain' means simple, unflavored food (`plain bagel`). 'Casual' describes relaxed everyday clothes, cafés, or chats (`casual lunch`).
quests.explanation: Natural — relaxed everyday dress and atmosphere earn 'casual'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ lunch" — starts with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Close' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Uncomfortably warm with little fresh air.
quests.contextSentence: One ___ nose makes breathing hard during winter colds.
quests.usageExample: A stuffy nose makes breathing hard during winter colds.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Close' covers cramped space (`close quarters`). 'Stuffy' describes stale indoor air OR pompous formal attitudes.
quests.explanation: Natural — warm indoor spaces lacking air feel 'stuffy'.
quests.hint: 'Close' covers cramped space (`close quarters`) — think of the 'Attic Room' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Clear' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Free from blame or wrongdoing.
quests.contextSentence: Witnesses proved the clerk was ___ of any mistake.
quests.usageExample: Witnesses proved the clerk was innocent of any mistake.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Clear' cleans consciences or paths (`clear name`). 'Innocent' declares zero crime or pure childlike honesty.
quests.explanation: Natural — legal lack of guilt requires 'innocent'.
quests.hint: 'Clear' cleans consciences or paths (`clear name`) — think of the 'Court Verdict' sense starting with 'I'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Eager' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Showing lively interest and energy.
quests.contextSentence: Young gardeners were ___ to join Saturday’s tree planting.
quests.usageExample: Young gardeners were enthusiastic to join Saturday’s tree planting.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Eager' looks forward impatiently (`eager to start`). 'Enthusiastic' shows loud, warm excitement (`enthusiastic applause`).
quests.explanation: Natural — warm, energetic applause takes 'enthusiastic'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ applause" — starts with 'E'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Willing' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Prepared or happy to agree when asked.
quests.contextSentence: Make sure every safety strap is ___ before takeoff.
quests.usageExample: Make sure every safety strap is ready before takeoff.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Willing' focuses on mindset consent (`willing helper`). 'Ready' focuses on practical preparation (`bags packed and ready`).
quests.explanation: Natural — practically prepared to move right now uses 'ready'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "bags packed and ___" — starts with 'R'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Bored' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Lacking excitement or interest.
quests.contextSentence: Without examples, long grammar talks quickly feel ___.
quests.usageExample: Without examples, long grammar talks quickly feel dull.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Bored' describes the PERSON feeling tired of waiting (`I am bored`). 'Dull' describes the THING causing boredom (`a dull speech`) or blunted color/knife.
quests.explanation: Natural — lifeless objects, colors, or lectures are 'dull'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "a ___ speech" — starts with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Crowd' in the sentence.
quests.definition: A group of people gathered together.
quests.contextSentence: The young violinist charmed the concert hall ___.
quests.usageExample: The young violinist charmed the concert hall audience.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Crowd' gathers anywhere (`street crowd`). 'Audience' specifically gathers to watch or listen to a show, talk, or book.
quests.explanation: Natural — listeners and spectators at shows form an 'audience'.
quests.hint: 'Crowd' gathers anywhere (`street crowd`) — think of the 'Theater Show' sense starting with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Friend' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Someone connected closely with you.
quests.contextSentence: Both chefs opened a bakery together as equal ___.
quests.usageExample: Both chefs opened a bakery together as equal partner.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Friend' shares warm personal trust. 'Partner' shares an active joint task, business, tennis match, or life bond.
quests.explanation: Natural — teammates in pairs, projects, or firms are a 'partner'.
quests.hint: 'Friend' shares warm personal trust — think of the 'Tennis Doubles' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Leader' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Someone who shows others the way.
quests.contextSentence: Read the quick setup ___ inside the speaker box.
quests.usageExample: Read the quick setup guide inside the speaker box.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Leader' directs decisions and inspires teams. 'Guide' leads visitors through unknown trails, museums, or manuals.
quests.explanation: Natural — leading tours and safety paths takes a 'guide'.
quests.hint: 'Leader' directs decisions and inspires teams — think of the 'Canyon Walk' sense starting with 'G'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Piece' in the sentence.
quests.definition: A portion cut from a bigger whole.
quests.contextSentence: Add a bright ___ of lemon into the iced water.
quests.usageExample: Add a bright slice of lemon into the iced water.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Piece' fits cake, news, wood, or puzzles (`puzzle piece`). 'Slice' strictly cuts thin flat wedges (`slice of pizza/bread`).
quests.explanation: Natural — thin flat food portions take 'slice'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ of pizza/bread" — starts with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Part' in the sentence.
quests.definition: One piece forming a whole.
quests.contextSentence: Check the sports ___ of Sunday’s morning paper.
quests.usageExample: Check the sports section of Sunday’s morning paper.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Part' fits machines, stories, or roles (`play a part`). 'Section' labels clean organized zones (`frozen section`, `chapter section`).
quests.explanation: Natural — organized aisles and document divisions use 'section'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "frozen ___" — starts with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Few' in the sentence.
quests.definition: A small number of items.
quests.contextSentence: Waiters brought ___ warm blankets out to the patio.
quests.usageExample: Waiters brought several warm blankets out to the patio.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Few' (without 'a') hints scarcity (`too few`), 'a few' = 2–3. 'Several' comfortably means around 3 to 6, more than two.
quests.explanation: Natural — three to six items comfortably fits 'several'.
quests.hint: 'Few' (without 'a') hints scarcity (`too few`), 'a few' = 2–3 — think of the 'Bookshelf' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Damage' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Injury or trouble done to something.
quests.contextSentence: Doctors ensure new tests cause no ___ to volunteers.
quests.usageExample: Doctors ensure new tests cause no harm to volunteers.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Damage' hits physical objects, roofs, or reputations (`storm damage`). 'Harm' hurts living health, feelings, or morale (`no harm done`).
quests.explanation: Natural — emotional/living well-being uses 'harm'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "no ___ done" — starts with 'H'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Fix' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To return something to good condition.
quests.contextSentence: Local teams work to ___ wetlands along the bay.
quests.usageExample: Local teams work to restore wetlands along the bay.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Fix' gets a broken switch running again. 'Restore' carefully brings old paintings, habitats, or trust back to original beauty.
quests.explanation: Natural — reviving heritage art, forests, or trust takes 'restore'.
quests.hint: 'Fix' gets a broken switch running again — think of the 'Old Painting' sense starting with 'R'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Hurt' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To feel steady physical pain.
quests.contextSentence: Your shoulders may ___ if your desk chair sits too high.
quests.usageExample: Your shoulders may ache if your desk chair sits too high.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Hurt' works for sudden sharp pain OR feelings (`hurt my pride`). 'Ache' specifically means dull, continuous soreness (`muscles ache`).
quests.explanation: Natural — dull persistent soreness uses 'ache'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "muscles ___" — starts with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Prove' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To show something is true.
quests.contextSentence: Rail officials called to ___ the new departure gate.
quests.usageExample: Rail officials called to confirm the new departure gate.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Prove' supplies mathematical or scientific proof (`prove the law`). 'Confirm' checks bookings, dates, or rumors cleanly (`confirm flight`).
quests.explanation: Natural — verifying reservations or facts takes 'confirm'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ flight" — starts with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Gain' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To get a permit, document, or item formally.
quests.contextSentence: Builders need city inspections before they ___ occupancy permits.
quests.usageExample: Builders need city inspections before they obtain occupancy permits.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Gain' adds weight, traction, or experience naturally (`gain weight`). 'Obtain' gets permits, forms, or rare goods through formal requests.
quests.explanation: Natural — official permits and documents require 'obtain'.
quests.hint: 'Gain' adds weight, traction, or experience naturally (`gain weight`) — think of the 'Permit Desk' sense starting with 'O'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Need' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To be without something helpful.
quests.contextSentence: Some remote valleys still ___ fast fiber internet.
quests.usageExample: Some remote valleys still lack fast fiber internet.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Need' states requirement (`plants need sun`). 'Lack' points out an empty gap where something should be (`lack experience`).
quests.explanation: Natural — noticing an empty gap takes 'lack'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ experience" — starts with 'L'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Notice' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To catch sight of something.
quests.contextSentence: Birdwatchers hope to ___ snowy owls along the marsh.
quests.usageExample: Birdwatchers hope to spot snowy owls along the marsh.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Notice' becomes aware mentally or visually (`notice a change`). 'Spot' suddenly catches sight of a small item or person in a crowd (`spot a friend`).
quests.explanation: Natural — catching a visual needle-in-a-haystack uses 'spot'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ a friend" — starts with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Mention' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To speak or write briefly about something.
quests.contextSentence: Inspectors took care to ___ every cracked window pane.
quests.usageExample: Inspectors took care to note every cracked window pane.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Mention' drops a point casually (`mention your name`). 'Note' highlights something carefully so people pay attention or write it down (`note the deadline`).
quests.explanation: Natural — pointing out key rules uses 'note'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ the deadline" — starts with 'N'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Agree' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To say yes to an idea or offer.
quests.contextSentence: Local farmers markets now ___ mobile card payments.
quests.usageExample: Local farmers markets now accept mobile card payments.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Agree' shares the same opinion (`agree with you`). 'Accept' says yes to an invitation, gift, payment, or apology (`accept cards`).
quests.explanation: Natural — saying yes to offers, cards, or apologies uses 'accept'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ cards" — starts with 'A'.
